content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text weighs the challenger's seed/loins chain against the defender's chain in a chain-versus-chain collision, so K-C governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D6 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.", "rule_words": "A link is judged by its support, never by whether any verse, or the chain as a whole, states it word for word; and a verse whose words leave the question open decides nothing by itself. When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse: I weighed whether the judge may penalize a footed chain for not explicitly naming Joseph or for resting on inference (forbidden by support-only judging) or whether such notes are merely chain-footing observations (allowed); the underdetermination uses the non-explicit naming/inference as reasons, so I read it as forbidden.", "why": "The judge calls footed chains underdetermined because one does not name Joseph and the other rests on an inference, using explicit-statement/inference objections rather than chain footing alone."}
